title: Brum and the Tiny Bat
markdown:
In the rocky highlands of Misty Kettle, wind whispered through old stones and the sky painted itself in a thousand blues and greys. Brum lived there: a young ogre, gentle as a falling feather. His skin was moss after spring rain. His eyes were two smooth grey river pebbles. He loved the quiet hum of the mountains, purple heather after a shower, and the steady drum of his own large heart.

His best friend was not another ogre, nor a grumbling goat. She was a bat no bigger than his thumb, wings thin as dried leaves. He had named her Whisper, for she was as light as a breath, and her squeaks were softer than fern-fronds. Wings like scraps of twilight, purple and indigo when the light caught them. She slept in the deep warm pocket of his tunic, tiny snores like the softest sigh.

One bright afternoon a cloud drifted by that looked exactly like a fluffy sheep in a floppy hat of mist. Brum sat on a sun-warmed boulder that felt like a giant hug. “Look, Whisper. A cloud-sheep with a jaunty cap. I do believe it’s off to visit the moon.”

Whisper peeked from the pocket, nose twitching. A gust smelling of pine and wild thyme tickled Brum’s nose. He sneezed a mighty Achooo that sent pebbles skittering, and turned to enjoy the breeze in his thick dark hair. When he looked back, the pocket was empty.

“Whisper?” He peered in. Soft lining. The other pocket, kept for shiny stones: nothing. Broad shoulders slumped. A cold little stone seemed to drop in his tummy. He looked under the boulder, behind prickly gorse, even in the clear bubbling stream, where every pebble showed. “Whisper!” His voice shook like a leaf. The wind sighed back, carrying only leaf-rustle. Knees wobbled. This was not a lost button. This was his quiet companion in a place big enough to swallow the sun. He needed help. Who could find a vanishing bat in all of Misty Kettle?

High on the tallest peak, in a tower that sometimes seemed mist and sometimes moonlight, lived Wizard Figwort: wise, though some whispered his memory was as scattered as dandelion seed. Still, Brum had heard of his kindly way of finding things truly lost. With a determined sigh he climbed. The path coiled like a snake. Air thinned, carrying the crisp scent of cold stone and distant snow. After a long time he reached weathered stones against blue sky. He knocked a gentle rap that echoed like a distant drum, soft enough not to startle birds.

The door creaked. A kindly face, beard tangled as a bird’s nest. Spectacles perched on the tip of his nose like tiny acrobats. “Hello! A potion? A spell for runaway socks? Mine wander off when one isn’t looking.”

Brum shuffled enormous feet. “My bat, Whisper, she’s gone. Vanished. She always stays in my pocket.”

Figwort blinked, pushing the spectacles further down. “A bat? Are you sure it wasn’t a particularly dark speedy butterfly? Or a very small quiet cloud that took a detour? I saw a peculiar one earlier, shaped like a teacup, but it had forgotten its handle.”

Brum described her: the pocket, the nose like a furry question mark, the chasing of dust motes in sunbeams. He did not want her to be just any lost thing.

The wizard rummaged: colourful pebbles, a half-eaten biscuit that looked squirrel-nibbled, a shiny button. Then an Aha, and a second pair of spectacles with thicker lenses.

“Whisper! Of course. Sometimes our dear little creatures aren’t lost at all. They’re simply exploring.” He pointed toward a window and a dense patch of ancient oaks. “Look. Fluttering among the highest branches, where the sunbeams play tag.”

Brum squinted, his big eyes straining past bright sunlight. At first only dappled light through green leaves, a pattern on the bark like a secret code. Then a flicker. A tiny shadow darting. Another. Nestled on a high branch, playing chase with a dappled sunbeam: Whisper. She wasn’t lost. She was exploring, little wings catching light like dark jewels against bright green. She looked so happy, so free, flitting between ancient oak leaves as if she owned the sky.

Relief warmed the cold stone in his chest. Figwort chuckled, dry leaves. “They have their own journeys, even if it’s only to the top of a tree. You gave her a safe warm home, so she felt brave enough to see what else the world offered. And she comes back.”

As if summoned, Whisper swooped, a tiny bell of a squeak, circled twice, and landed in Brum’s outstretched hand. She nuzzled his thumb. He felt her heart against his skin.

They did not hurry the oak. Leaves shimmered like emeralds. Sunbeams still played tag, slower now. Whisper tucked herself into the pocket again, a small weight against Brum’s ribs, and he started down. No dreadful chase through dark forests. A misunderstanding that turned into a discovery, and a happy reunion. The moss-green hills, the deep blue sky, the fiery orange of the setting sun casting long shadows: they glowed with quiet joy. The mountain wind, whispering through the stones, seemed to carry not only secrets but a gentle happy hum, a song of companionship as vast and peaceful as the highlands themselves.
characters: Brum (gentle young ogre), Whisper (a tiny pocket-bat)
